content: 1. Initiating ozanimod is generally not recommended in patients who are concurrently receiving medications that prolong the QT interval and have known arrhythmogenic properties. 2. Pentamidine and pasireotide both increase the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified, and patients should be closely monitored. 3. Pazopanib and pentamidine both prolong the QTc interval. Therapy adjustments and close monitoring are advised. 4. Pentamidine increases peramivir levels by reducing renal clearance. Caution is advised, and monitoring is recommended. 5. Exercise caution when peramivir is co-administered with nephrotoxic drugs. 6. Pentamidine and potassium citrate/citric acid both elevate serum potassium levels. Use caution and monitor closely. 7. Quetiapine and pentamidine each increase the toxicity of the other by prolonging the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 8. Avoid using pentamidine with drugs that prolong the QT interval in patients with risk factors for QT prolongation. Postmarketing cases have reported QT prolongation with overdose in patients with concomitant illnesses or drugs causing electrolyte imbalance or QT prolongation. 9. Pentamidine and quinine both increase the QTc interval. Caution and close monitoring are required. 10. Quizartinib and pentamidine enhance each other's effects by prolonging the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified, and patients should be closely monitored. 11. Patients co-administered QT-prolonging drugs should undergo more frequent ECG monitoring. 12. Rilpivirine increases pentamidine toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are advised. 13. Rilpivirine should be used cautiously when co-administered with drugs that carry a known risk of Torsades de Pointes. 14. Rucaparib increases pentamidine levels or effects by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP2C19 metabolism. Therapy adjustments and close monitoring are necessary. 15. Dosage adjustments of CYP2C19 substrates should be considered if clinically indicated. 16. Selpercatinib increases pentamidine toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are required. 17. Pentamidine reduces the effects of sodium picosulfate/magnesium oxide/anhydrous citric acid by altering metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 18. Co-administration with antibiotics reduces efficacy by altering colonic bacterial flora needed to convert sodium picosulfate to its active form. 19. Sorafenib and pentamidine both prolong the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 20. Sparsentan increases pentamidine levels or effects by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP2C19 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 21. Sparsentan, a CYP2C19 inducer, reduces exposure to CYP2C19 substrates and diminishes their efficacy. 22. Stiripentol increases pentamidine levels or effects by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP2C19 metabolism. Therapy adjustments and close monitoring are necessary. 23. Consider reducing the dose of CYP2C19 substrates if adverse reactions occur when co-administered with stiripentol. 24. Pentamidine and streptozocin both increase nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Caution and monitoring are required. 25. Pentamidine and tacrolimus both increase nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 26. Pentamidine increases tazemetostat levels or effects by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 27. Tecovirimat increases pentamidine levels or effects by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP2C19 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are required. 28. Tecovirimat is a weak inhibitor of CYP2C8 and CYP2C19. Monitor for adverse effects if co-administered with sensitive substrates of these enzymes. 29. Pentamidine and teicoplanin both increase nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 30. Pentamidine and tenofovir DF both increase nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Caution and monitoring are required. Co-administration may also elevate tenofovir levels. 31. Pentamidine increases tinidazole levels or effects by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 32. Tipranavir and pentamidine each increase the toxicity of the other by prolonging the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 33. Increased risk of PR or QT prolongation and cardiac arrhythmias is associated with this combination. 34. Triclabendazole and pentamidine both prolong the QTc interval. Triclabendazole increases pentamidine levels or effects by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP2C19 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are required. 35. Trimethoprim and pentamidine both elevate serum potassium levels. Caution and monitoring are advised. Trimethoprim reduces urinary potassium excretion, potentially causing hyperkalemia, especially with high doses, renal insufficiency, or concurrent use of other hyperkalemia-inducing drugs. 36. Triptorelin increases pentamidine toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are necessary. This combination increases the risk of Torsades de Pointes. 37. Valbenazine and pentamidine both prolong the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are required. 38. Voclosporin and pentamidine both elevate serum potassium levels. Either drug increases the effects of the other by prolonging the QTc interval. Either drug also increases the toxicity of the other by causing nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Therapy adjustments and close monitoring are necessary. 39. Co-administration with nephrotoxic drugs may increase the risk of acute and/or chronic nephrotoxicity. 40. Acyclovir and pentamidine both increase nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. The significance of this interaction is unknown. 41. Adefovir and pentamidine both increase nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. The significance of this interaction is unknown. 42. Capreomycin and pentamidine both increase nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. The significance of this interaction is unknown. 43. Cephaloridine and pentamidine both increase nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. The significance of this interaction is unknown. 44. Chloroquine increases pentamidine toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. The significance of this interaction is unknown. 45. Colistin and pentamidine both increase nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. The significance of this interaction is unknown. 46. Didanosine and pentamidine each increase the toxicity of the other through pharmacodynamic synergy. The significance of this interaction is unknown. This combination enhances the risk of pancreatitis. 47. Pentamidine and entecavir each increase the effects of the other by reducing renal clearance. The significance of this interaction is unknown. Co-administration with drugs that reduce renal function or compete for active tubular secretion may increase serum concentrations of either entecavir or the co-administered drug. 48. Pentamidine reduces folic acid levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This applies only to the oral form of both agents. The significance of this interaction is unknown. 49. Foscarnet and pentamidine both increase nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. This interaction is due to pharmacodynamic synergy. The significance of this interaction is unknown. This combination increases the risk of severe hypocalcemia. 50. Ganciclovir increases pentamidine toxicity through pharmacodynamic synergy. The significance of this interaction is unknown. 51. Gentamicin and pentamidine both increase nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. The significance of this interaction is unknown. 52. Pentamidine reduces L-methylfolate levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This applies only to the oral form of both agents. The significance of this interaction is unknown. 53. Methoxyflurane and pentamidine both increase nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. The significance of this interaction is unknown. 54. Paromomycin and pentamidine both increase nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. The significance of this interaction is unknown. 55. Pentamidine and polymyxin B both increase nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. The significance of this interaction is unknown. 56. Pentamidine increases ruxolitinib levels or effects by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. The significance of this interaction is unknown. 57. Pentamidine increases ruxolitinib topical levels or effects by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. The significance of this interaction is unknown. 58. Pentamidine and streptomycin both increase nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. The significance of this interaction is unknown. 59. Pentamidine and tobramycin both increase nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. The significance of this interaction is unknown. 60. Valganciclovir increases pentamidine toxicity through pharmacodynamic synergy. The significance of this interaction is unknown. 61. Pentamidine and vancomycin both increase nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. The significance of this interaction is unknown. 62. Zidovudine increases pentamidine toxicity through pharmacodynamic synergy. The significance of this interaction is unknown.
